entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Friedrich Alexander Graf von der Pahlen was a Baltic German diplomat and administrator born in 1825 in Pahlen, Livonia (now Pėtnē, Latvia), and died on January 20, 1863. He served as the Russian Governor of Estonia and Latvia from 1860 to 1863. Von der Pahlen was a key figure in the Baltic German aristocracy and played a significant role in the region's governance during the mid-19th century.

Von der Pahlen's tenure was marked by significant economic and cultural developments in the region, including the expansion of the Baltic German railway network and the establishment of the Livonian Baroque Museum. His leadership also oversaw the construction of several public buildings, including the Pahlen Manor and the Pahlen Palace.

The legacy of Friedrich von der Pahlen can be seen in the modern-day cultural and historical heritage of the region, with many of the public buildings he oversaw still standing today. His commitment to preserving the cultural identity of the Baltic German region continues to be celebrated by locals and historians alike.

Friedrich von der Pahlen's contributions to the region's governance and cultural development make him a notable figure in the history of Estonia and Latvia.
